talking_points.headline: HSBC to shut German transaction-services unit, cutting 300+ jobs by 2028
talking_points.context_html: HSBC confirmed it will wind down its Dusseldorf transaction-services business, following last year's sale of HSBC Germany's private-banking arm to BNP Paribas. This is a live case study inside Adam's own organisation: a back-office function being exited rather than automated, which sharpens the question of whether HSBC's AI investment (Wealth Intelligence, the Google Cloud partnership) is being aimed at saving functions like this one, or simply at managing their wind-down.
source_links: HSBC to Wind Down German Transaction Services

talking_points.headline: Pentagon contract row shows Anthropic will walk away from a client over AI governance
talking_points.context_html: FOIA documents reveal Anthropic refused Pentagon terms that would have allowed unrestricted deployment on classified networks, prompting Pete Hegseth, U.S. Defense Secretary to formally designate Anthropic a 'supply chain risk' in February. For Adam, this is a real precedent for the AI-vendor governance conversations already live inside HSBC around Google Cloud and OpenAI-powered tools: a frontier lab is willing to lose a major customer over values-based restrictions, which is exactly the kind of risk banks now need to price into their own AI vendor contracts.
source_links: AI Giants Work Hand-in-Hand With the Pentagon

talking_points.headline: DBS hit with ~US$1 billion 1MDB-linked lawsuit despite top-ranked wealth franchise
talking_points.context_html: DBS is fighting a S$1.298 billion claim from liquidators of four 1MDB-linked companies, the latest legal tail from the scandal that has dogged the region's private banking industry for over a decade. It's a reminder that legacy AML/KYC exposure remains a live tail-risk even for a franchise as well-regarded as DBS's, and reinforces why HSBC's own source-of-wealth and KYC controls need to stay ahead of, not just compliant with, regulatory expectations.
source_links: DBS sued for US$1 billion in 1MDB-linked claim

HSBC News.title: HSBC to wind down German transaction-services business, cutting 300+ jobs by 2028
HSBC News.summary: HSBC confirmed it will shut its Dusseldorf-based transaction-services operations, affecting more than 300 roles across HSBC Transaction Services GmbH and HSBC Service Company Germany GmbH, phased out by 2028. The move follows HSBC Germany's sale of its private-banking business to BNP Paribas last year, as the bank narrows its footprint to focus on areas of competitive advantage.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Singapore's DBS sued for ~US$1 billion in alleged 1MDB-linked claim
Competitor Intelligence.summary: DBS is being sued for S$1.298 billion (~US$1.03bn) by liquidators of four companies linked to the 1MDB scandal, including BlackRock Commodities (Global) and Platinum Global Luxury Services. DBS says it will fight the claim vigorously and has made no provision for it. The suit is the latest in a long-running, multibillion-dollar global effort to recover 1MDB-linked assets.

AI & Technology.title: FOIA documents reveal Anthropic refused Pentagon terms, was branded a 'supply chain risk'
AI & Technology.summary: Newly disclosed FOIA documents show OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI each signed July 2025 Pentagon contracts worth up to $200 million to prototype military decision-making tools. The Pentagon reportedly asked OpenAI for a version of its model designed to refuse requests as rarely as possible, while Anthropic refused terms permitting unrestricted deployment on classified networks unless its autonomous-weapons and domestic-surveillance restrictions were kept — leading Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to formally designate Anthropic a 'supply chain risk' in February.

AI & Technology.title: Meta launches Muse, a paid personal AI agent that acts on users' behalf
AI & Technology.summary: Meta unveiled Muse, a proactive AI agent that books tickets, schedules appointments and executes multi-step tasks rather than just answering questions, available free or via $20/$100-a-month tiers. It runs on a dedicated secure VM and is designed to be long-running and personalised, marking Meta's push into agentic, task-executing AI for consumers.
